summary: Defines L2TPv3 extensions to set up TDM pseudowires, both structure-agnostic and structure-aware in the CESoPSN style. It lets L2TPv3 carry circuit-style traffic over packet networks.

plainLanguage.summary: Old circuit lines can be sent across a modern network if both ends first agree on setup. This is the agreement process using L2TPv3.

questions: what is the l2tpv3 tdm pw avp
what does l2tpv3 result code 30 mean
subtitle: How two L2TPv3 endpoints agree on the details before carrying T1, E1, T3 or E3 circuits over a packet network.

tldr.problem: Time-Division Multiplexing (TDM) circuits such as E1 and T1 can be emulated over packet networks, but the two ends must agree on the circuit type, bit rate, payload size and header options before any data flows.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds two Attribute-Value Pairs to L2TPv3, a TDM PW AVP (type 99) and an RTP AVP (type 100), plus new pseudowire type values and a new Result Code 30 with five error codes for mismatches.
tldr.outcome: It covers structure-agnostic (SAToP) and CESoPSN-style structure-aware pseudowires. Setup of TDMoIP-style pseudowires is left for further study.

today: RFC 5611 is a Proposed Standard from August 2009. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 5611 extends the Layer Two Tunneling Protocol version 3 (L2TPv3, RFC 3931) so it can set up TDM pseudowires. These are two kinds: structure-agnostic ones, defined in RFC 4553, and structure-aware ones in the CESoPSN style, defined in RFC 5086.

Setup of structure-aware pseudowires using the encapsulations of RFC 5087 (TDMoIP) is left for further study. The matching setup for MPLS networks using LDP is in RFC 5287.

One data-plane rule is repeated here: the order of the CESoPSN Control Word and the RTP header (if used) MUST match between TDM data packets and CE signaling packets.
sections.plainLanguage: Old phone-style lines can be sent over a computer network. This document is the handshake that two ends use to agree on how, using one existing tunnel system.

sections.title: What Changes in L2TPv3 Itself
sections.content:
The L2TPv3 control connection sets up and tears down pseudowire sessions and carries end point status. Tear-down of a TDM pseudowire follows Section 3.4.3 of RFC 3931.

Because the attachment circuit status is already carried in the data plane by RFC 4553 and RFC 5086, the Set-Link-Info (SLI) message SHOULD NOT be used for it. The Circuit Status AVP in ICRQ and ICRP messages MUST always have both the N and A bits set.

A control connection that supports TDM pseudowires MUST add the right PW Type values to its Pseudowire Capabilities List AVP. TDM pseudowires have their own Control Word, which acts as a dedicated L2-Specific Sublayer, so the L2-Specific Sublayer AVP MUST be omitted or set to 0. They also do their own sequencing, so the Data Sequencing AVP MUST be omitted or set to 0.
sections.plainLanguage: Most of the old tunnel rules stay the same. A few messages are skipped because the circuit already carries that information itself.

sections.title: The TDM PW AVP
sections.content:
The TDM PW AVP (Attribute Type 99, length 12 before hiding) goes in ICRQ and OCRQ messages. It MAY be hidden and its M bit SHOULD be 0. It has four settings.

Bit Rate is the rate of the local attachment circuit in units of 64 Kbit/s, as an unsigned 16-bit integer. For structure-agnostic emulation it MUST be 32 for E1, 24 for basic-mode T1 (25 for Octet-aligned T1), 535 for E3 and 699 for T3. For CESoPSN it MUST be the number of DS0 channels. The values 24 and 25 for T1 are for convenience and are not the exact rate.

Payload Bytes is the number of TDM payload bytes per packet. Any value may be used for structure-agnostic emulation. For CESoPSN it MUST be a whole multiple of the number of DS0 channels. For trunk-specific NxDS0 with CAS, the trunk frames per multiframe fragment MUST be a whole divisor of the frames per trunk multiframe.

The two-bit SP field says how CE application signaling travels: 01 for a data PW expecting signaling in a separate PW, 10 for the signaling PW, 11 for one PW with both, and 00 for SAToP or CESoPSN without separate signaling. The two-bit CAS field is 01 for an E1 trunk, 10 for T1/ESF, 11 for T1/SF, and 00 otherwise. Reserved bits MUST be 0 on sending and ignored on receipt.
sections.plainLanguage: The first note says what kind of line it is, how fast it is, how many bytes go in each packet, and whether warning signals travel separately.

sections.title: The RTP AVP
sections.content:
The RTP AVP (Attribute Type 100, length 16 before hiding) may appear in ICRQ, OCRQ, ICRP and OCRP. Its presence means the pseudowire uses an RTP header. Whether RTP is used MUST match in both directions. It MAY be hidden and its M bit SHOULD be 0.

The D bit selects differential timestamping when 1 and absolute timestamping when 0, and each direction can choose independently. The C bit gives the header order: when 1, the RTP header comes after the Control Word, the mode RFC 4553 and RFC 5086 describe for L2TPv3 demultiplexing; when 0, it comes before the Control Word, the old mode described in their appendices.

PT is the expected RTP payload type, and 0 means the receiver does not check it. Timestamp Clock Frequency is in units of 8 KHz. SSRC is the expected synchronization source ID, and 0 means it is not used to detect misconnections. Since L2TP cookies give another safeguard, if the cookie length is above 0 the SSRC SHOULD be 0.
sections.plainLanguage: The second note is optional. It says whether each packet also carries a clock stamp, and it says which way the labels are stacked.

sections.title: Creating the Session and Handling Mismatches
sections.content:
An LCCE that wants a TDM pseudowire session MUST put the TDM PW AVP in the ICRQ or OCRQ, and the RTP AVP if and only if RTP is used. The peer checks the TDM PW AVP and whether it can meet the RTP requirements, then replies with ICRP or OCRP, including a matching RTP AVP if needed. The initiator in turn checks that it can meet what the reply asks for.

The two peers MUST agree on the TDM PW AVP values. If they do not, the session is refused with Result Code 30 and an Error Code that names the problem (listed in the table below).

If CE signaling for a basic CESoPSN PW goes in its own PW instance, the two PWs MUST use the same PW type, the same values in every TDM AVP field except SP (01 for data, 10 for signaling), and either both use RTP or neither does.
sections.plainLanguage: If the two notes do not match, the answer is a polite no with a number that says which part was wrong.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content:
IANA assigned six L2TPv3 pseudowire types: 0x0011 structure-agnostic E1, 0x0012 T1 (DS1), 0x0013 E3, 0x0014 T3 (DS3), 0x0015 CESoPSN basic mode and 0x0017 CESoPSN TDM with CAS. These match the MPLS pseudowire types in RFC 4446.

It also assigned AVP IDs 99 (TDM Pseudowire AVP) and 100 (RTP AVP), Result Code 30 for the CDN message, and a new registry of TDM-specific Error Codes inside the Result Code AVP values. Further values are assigned by Expert Review.
sections.plainLanguage: Each kind of line and each note gets an official number, kept in a public list.

sections.title: Congestion Control and Security
sections.content:
The congestion considerations of RFC 4553 and RFC 5086 apply to the structure-agnostic and CESoPSN modes respectively.

This document covers only the L2TPv3 control plane for setup, so it adds no security considerations beyond those of RFC 3931. Data plane security for TDM pseudowires is discussed in RFC 4553 and RFC 5086, and the L2TPv3 data plane adds security mechanisms based on cookies.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new to worry about here. The older documents already cover traffic jams and safety, and tunnel cookies help too.
